rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes heating and mechanical testing with in situ characterization, while the target uses molecular-dynamics simulations varying composition and temperature. These are fundamentally different kinds of study (experimental vs. simulation), so the intervention does not match.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies isothermal tests at 673–1073 K and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, whereas the target uses MD simulations from 300–1200 K at a strain rate of 1e8 s^-1. The temperature ranges overlap only partially, and the strain rates differ by many orders of magnitude, so the conditions are not the same.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a slip-mode transition to edge dislocations with thermal super-jogging, while the target explains behavior via solid-solution strengthening, lattice mismatch, and dislocation mobility changes without a slip-mode transition. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a yield strength plateau at elevated temperatures, whereas the target predicts and finds a continuous decrease in strength with temperature. The predicted outcomes are contradictory in direction.
